gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow caps each DELTA 3 Plus input at 15 A, so each input reaches 500 W only from a panel string working at 33.3 V or more and staying under 60 V open-circuit. By the same arithmetic, the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2's single 20 A input needs at least 50 V of working voltage under a 60 V ceiling to reach 1,000 W, which Notebookcheck says is difficult in practice.
standout_why: I compared four pages. Volt & Valley (the cited rival) gives '1,000W ... two separate 500W MPPT inputs' but no voltage window and no amps. It also pairs the station with 440 W of panels. Our current Dealectric page gives '11–60 V, 15 A' and a Voc warning, but it never turns 15 A into a minimum panel voltage, and it calls the Elite's 20 A single input fine for 'two panels in parallel' without checking that against the 60 V cap. EcoFlow's DELTA 3 series page says only '500W MPPT × 2'. ChatGPT's own answer offered the Elite 100 V2 as a full 1,000 W alternative, with no hint that one 12–60 V / 20 A input makes 1,000 W hard to reach. None of these pages states EcoFlow's rule that a panel over any one limit 'cannot be used', the 33.3 V-per-input minimum, or the 50 V minimum for the Elite.
decides: This confirms the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus as the pick and sets what panels the plan needs. To get 1,000 W the shopper needs two separate strings of about 500 W, one per input. Each string must work at 33.3 V or more (500 W ÷ 15 A), have a cold-weather Voc of 60 V or less, and stay at 15 A or less. That rules out paralleling two 20 V-class panels into one input, since EcoFlow's own example (12.9 A × 2 = 25.8 A) is refused, and it rules out putting two 40 V-class panels in series. It also removes the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 as an equal alternative. Its one input needs at least 50 V at 20 A while staying under 60 V Voc, and Notebookcheck works out that two BLUETTI PV350s can't go in series (2 × 46.5 V = 93 V), leaving about 700 W.

findings.label: Solar input limits per input, and EcoFlow's rule for when a panel can be used
findings.value: 11–60 V, 15 A max, 500 W max per input. Panel Voc must be inside the voltage range, panel current must not exceed 15 A, and panel power must not exceed 500 W. EcoFlow: 'All three conditions must be met; exceeding any one of them means the solar panels cannot be used.'
